summary: OAuth2 device-code flow from private IdP with client mTLS CN suffix results in scheduled-worker RBAC denials
description: Issue summary: Customer uses OAuth2 device-code flow for long-running scheduled workers that cannot provide interactive redirects. The upstream private IdP is configured to require mutual TLS for token requests; client certificates are issued with a CN that includes a tenant suffix (example: service-account-42@nimbledocs). Impact: Scheduled workers intermittently receive 403 when attempting service actions that require tenant-scoped roles. Affected jobs are critical nightly ingestion workers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a private deployment with the customer's IdP using device-code/OAuth2 device flow and mTLS token endpoint.
2) Issue device codes via /device_authorization endpoint and complete user consent on a separate device.
3) Customer's token-exchange client performs mTLS TLS handshake to IdP token endpoint; client cert CN is 'service-account-42@nimbledocs'.
4) Token introspection in Redwood's private control plane returns an actor identifier based on client certificate subject, which is forwarded to the RBAC service.
5) Scheduled worker attempts to call admin-proxied endpoints and receives 403 due to missing tenant role bindings.
6) Reproducible ~40% of the time; other attempts succeed when client cert CN lacks suffix or when a different cert is used.
observed_behavior: When the mTLS client certificate CN includes a tenant delimiter suffix ('@nimbledocs') the identity extraction routine maps the principal to 'service-account-42' and separately records a domain suffix. RBAC lookup fails to find tenant-scoped role bindings because the tenant suffix is not preserved in the claim/key used to resolve cross-tenant bindings. Result: ephemeral access tokens introspect as valid but authorization returns 403 for tenant-scoped operations.
expected_behavior: Principal canonicalization should consistently preserve the tenant-scoped principal string used by the customer's RBAC bindings. Device-flow workers should be authorized when the certificate maps to a known service account with appropriate tenant role bindings.
logs: 2026-03-09T23:14:02Z idp-token-introspect request_id=ab12cd actor_cn="service-account-42@nimbledocs" ; introspect_result=active ; principal=service-account-42 ; tenant_hint=nimbledocs
2026-03-09T23:14:02Z rbac-lookup trace_id=xyz123 resolved_key=service-account-42 (no tenant namespace) -> no match in tenant-scoped binding table
2026-03-09T23:14:02Z gateway response 403 request_id=ab12cd reason="tenant role missing for principal service-account-42"
investigation_notes: Support triage: reproduced in customer's staging by replaying mTLS handshake with a test cert that includes suffix - observed same 403 behavior.
Hypothesis 1: Identity proxy strips or splits CN on '@' and our RBAC lookup path expects a namespaced key 'nimbledocs/service-account-42'.

Hypothesis 2: Device-flow token exchange path uses a different claim normalization codepath than interactive OIDC flows; mismatch causes tenant hint to be attached as a separate attribute rather than part of the canonical principal string.
Checked logs: the auth-proxy attaches tenant_hint metadata but downstream RBAC service receives only principal string without namespace (see logs).
Temporary artifact uploaded to support bucket: s3://redwood-support/nimbledocs/deviceflow-mtls-replay-20260309.tar.gz
Related configuration: IdP sends client cert CN as full string; customer's SCIM/RBAC bindings are configured using fully namespaced principal keys 'nimbledocs/service-account-42'.
workaround: Customer can provision a second client certificate with CN stripped (service-account-42) and rotate the device-flow client to use that cert for token exchanges. Alternatively, modify RBAC bindings to include the un-namespaced principal 'service-account-42' as a temporary grant.
